title: serving-runtime-weekly-update-kernel-kv-batching-2026-03-31
content:
Week of 2026-03-30 - Serving Runtime Weekly Update
Owner: Alyssa Chen (eng-serving-runtime)
Status: Draft

Summary:
- This week focused on three cross-cutting areas: kernel selection and micro-optimizations, KV cache stability and telemetry, and batching logic improvements (continuous batching + adaptive sizing). Several PRs landed in staging; a couple of regressions were identified and are being triaged.

Wins / Highlights:
- Kernel autotuner prototype (PR #1427) landed behind a flag; initial microbenchmarks show ~6-8% CPU reduction for causal attention on longer sequences (2k tokens) on A100.
- KV cache telemetry added: hot-prefix hit-rate, per-route cold-fill latency histograms, and eviction churn metric. Early dashboards allow us to see that 12% of requests are benefiting from prefix reuse across routes.
- Batcher change (PR #1452) to increase max batch-formation window from 10ms to 15ms for low-QPS routes improved throughput by ~10% without measurable p95 regression in our synthetic bench.

Kernel work (lead: Samir Patel)
- What we did:
  - Merged initial kernel selection table and autotuner backend (flag: kernel-autotune-v1). Autotuner picks between fused attention kernels and fallback based on sequence length distribution sampled over a 5-minute window.
  - Implemented light-weight runtime counters to track kernel hot/cold switches to avoid oscillation.
  - Landed micro-op rewrite for rotary embedding math to reduce memory copies (bench: -3% latency for short sequences).
- Observations:
  - On small batch sizes (<4), fused kernels sometimes underperform due to extra setup costs; autotuner currently biases toward fused for long sequences but needs a batch-size-aware heuristic.
  - Kernel switch churn observed when traffic mixes short (chat) and long (document) requests; counter hysteresis is doing OK but we should add a minimum residency time to avoid frequent churn.
- Next steps:
  - Add batch-size dimension to autotuner decision table (Samir, week+1).
  - Run 24h traffic replay with mixed workloads to validate autotuner thresholds (Jordan to own).

KV cache (lead: Jordan Lee)
- What we did:
  - Deployed prefix-level KV cache telemetry (hit-rate, cold-fill latency) to staging dashboards.
  - Fixed a bug where eviction could race with async prefetch, causing KV read NPEs under heavy churn (PR #1452 hotfix).
  - Experimented with LFU-style aging vs LRU: LFU gives slightly better long-tail hit-rate for multi-tenant traffic where a few prefixes are very hot.
- Observations:
  - Hot-prefixes (top 1%) account for ~40% of all cache hits; tail prefixes (<10 requests/day) are high churn and cause most eviction activity.
  - Cold-fill tail latency spike at p99 when concurrent prefetches occur; prefetch dedup logic helps but still susceptible when many tiny prefixes are requested simultaneously.
- Blockers / Risks:
  - Prefetch dedup edge-case still causing duplicated DB/remote calls in rare race; risk of increased upstream load during synthetic traffic spikes.
- Next steps:
  - Implement singleflight-style dedup for prefetches (Priya to prototype).
  - Add adaptive prefetch backoff when upstream error rates increase (Diego).
  - Plan a canary rollout of LFU-variant to 5% of traffic for 48 hours.

Batching (lead: Priya Kumar)
- What we did:
  - Tuned continuous batching parameters: increased max window for low-QPS routes, lowered minimum fill requirement for high-latency-sensitive routes.
  - Added simulation harness to replay real traffic traces and compare latency/throughput tradeoffs offline.
  - Implemented a metric to surface batch-utilization vs latency percentiles per route.
- Observations:
  - For enterprise routes with bursty traffic, an adaptive window performed better than static windows (avg throughput +12%, p95 latency unchanged).
  - For extremely latency-sensitive routes (SLOs < 80ms), batching still harmful; we should support an explicit route-level config to disable batching.
- Next steps:
  - Wire route-level batching controls into Console so customers can toggle (product partner scoping meeting scheduled).
  - Run long-duration replay with mixed-route configs to fine-tune defaults.

Metrics & Experiments:
- Staging benchmark summary (mixed workload replay, 8xA100):
  - Baseline (no autotuner, old batching): p50 42ms, p95 210ms, p99 490ms, tokens/sec 18k
  - With kernel-autotune + batching-tuning: p50 40ms, p95 200ms, p99 460ms, tokens/sec 19.8k
  - KV cache canary (LFU) expected to raise hit-rate from 28% -> ~34% on canary tenants.
- Note: numbers are synthetic; we will validate on a non-synthetic production canary next week.

Standup / Meeting notes (this week):
- Monday: Kernel autotuner design walkthrough; agreed to add batch-size dimension and residency hysteresis. Action: Samir to update design doc.
- Wednesday: KV cache incident postmortem (short-lived NPE); root cause: race between eviction and prefetch cancellation. Agreed fix and backport (hotfix merged).
- Friday: Batching tuning review with product; product asked for route-level toggle and safety defaults.

Blockers / Help needed:
- Need SRE on-call time to run a 24h mixed-traffic replay against staging GPUs and collect kernel-switch telemetry (requesting Diego + SRE scheduling).
- Need access to per-tenant traffic traces for 30-day window to better tune LFU thresholds (privacy gating required from security).

Decisions made:
- Autotuner will remain behind feature flag for two weeks and be rolled to canary tenants only.
- KV cache LFU experiment to 5% of traffic for 48 hours, monitor upstream load and cold-fill p99.
- Batch window default increased to 15ms for routes with QPS < 5; provide route-level override in Console.

Action items / Owners (next week):
- Samir: Add batch-size dimension + residency hysteresis to autotuner (ETA: 2026-04-07).
- Jordan: Run 24h mixed-traffic replay and report kernel switch churn and perf deltas (ETA: 2026-04-03).
- Priya: Prototype prefetch singleflight and run canary for LFU variant (ETA: 2026-04-07).
- Diego: Coordinate SRE for staging replay and own adaptive prefetch backoff work (ETA: 2026-04-08).
- Alyssa: Draft rollout playbook for kernel-autotune and KV-LFU canary (ETA: 2026-04-05).

Attachments / Links:
- PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1427, https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1452
- Design doc: confluence://redwood/pages/serving-runtime-kv-caching-design
- JIRA: JIRA-RINF-3278 (kernel-autotune), JIRA-RINF-3301 (kv-prefetch-race)

Notes to self / informal:
- Follow up with infra on driver version mismatch that caused slight perf skew on one node last week.
- Consider adding a nightly job to compute per-route prefix reuse heatmaps to inform cache sizing.

End of update.
